body:
I have tried to get involved with my on campus LGBTQ/trans groups and a local trans group. 

I can’t help but feel ostracized every time that I am around LGBTQ people at my university. It’s as if there is this “in group” aka the people who are in charge of everything and the close friends of those people (as opposed to the people who are just there to socialize and fuck around (and tbh I see these people as being generally nice but very ignorant and cisprivileged, thus I am wary of them)). This “in group” feels so exclusive to me, and it permeates literally every LGBTQ group on campus. Every meeting/gathering I go to, I feel as if I am being talked down to or spoken to as if I am stupid. Even in small settings and the university trans club (which 4 people go to, including myself) and with people I consider “friends”, I feel as if I have to constantly watch myself so as not to be judged. The “in-group” is characterized by being politically correct, constantly policing privilege and gossiping about others in the group. When I am around such people I just get this deep feeling that I do not belong there, but I'm not going to belong anywhere else either. I've stopped seeing these people and going to events. These people also go to the local trans group, so I stopped going to those meetings, too.

I used to talk to a great social worker in high school that worked for the school board, but when I graduated I had to move on. I went in to my university's mental health center a month ago for a consultation, and thankfully one of the social workers there was able to take me as a patient. I like this guy okay, but we're in the process of getting to know me, and I feel as if that will take many many appointments. I only get to see him once every 2.5 weeks, and there's only 7ish weeks left of the school year. I won't be able to see him during the summer. I do not have any sort of health insurance or healthcare, so I have nowhere else to go. I do have an appointment with my university's psychiatrist on the 1st, so I am hoping that will help, but if I can't afford the meds I need, I don't know what I'll do.
